sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    E2E SYSTEM METRICS                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  LATENCY PERCENTILES
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Why percentiles? Averages hide outliers.

  Example: 100 requests
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  P50 (median) = 800ms   → Half of users wait < 800ms       │
  │  P95           = 3200ms  → 95% of users wait < 3.2s        │
  │  P99           = 8500ms  → 99% wait < 8.5s (worst cases)   │
  │  Average       = 1100ms  → Misleading! Hides P99 problem    │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  SLA Scoring:
  If SLA = 5000ms and your P95 = 3200ms → Score = 1.0 ✅
  If SLA = 5000ms and your P95 = 7000ms → Score = 0.6 ⚠️

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  COST PER QUERY
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  GPT-4o pricing (example):
  Input:  $5.00 / 1M tokens
  Output: $15.00 / 1M tokens

  Query uses 2000 input + 500 output tokens:
  Cost = (2000 × $5/1M) + (500 × $15/1M)
       = $0.010 + $0.0075
       = $0.0175 per query

  At 10,000 queries/day → $175/day → $5,250/month

  Cost efficiency score:
  Budget = $0.01/query
  Actual = $0.0175 → Score = max(0, 1 - (0.0175-0.01)/0.01) = 0.25 ❌

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  SUCCESS RATE vs RETRY RATE
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Success Rate = successful requests / total requests
  Target: > 0.95 (95%)

  Retry Rate = requests needing ≥1 retry / total requests
  Target: < 0.10 (10%)

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  CONTEXT UTILIZATION
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Context window: 128,000 tokens
  Avg tokens used: 45,000

  Utilization = 45,000 / 128,000 = 35%

  Too low (< 20%) → Wasting retrieval opportunity
  Too high (> 90%) → Risk of truncation errors
  Ideal: 30% – 70%
```

# 📊 LLM-as-Judge — How It Works

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LLM-AS-JUDGE PATTERN                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  WHY LLM-AS-JUDGE?
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Traditional metrics (ROUGE, F1) FAIL for open-ended answers:

  Question:    "Explain photosynthesis"
  Ground Truth:"Photosynthesis converts sunlight to glucose"
  Answer:      "Plants use solar energy to produce sugar via
                chlorophyll-driven chemical reactions"

  ROUGE-L:  0.12  ❌ (different words but CORRECT!)
  Token F1: 0.20  ❌ (same problem)
  LLM Judge: 0.90 ✅ (understands meaning, not just words)

  HOW LLM-AS-JUDGE WORKS:
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  1. SINGLE SCORING:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Prompt: "Rate the faithfulness from 0-1. Return JSON." │
  │  Judge:  {"score": 0.92, "explanation": "..."}          │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  2. PAIRWISE COMPARISON:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Prompt: "Which answer is better: A or B?"              │
  │  Judge:  {"winner": "A", "reason": "More complete"}     │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  3. RUBRIC-BASED:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  1.0 = All claims supported by context                  │
  │  0.7 = Most claims supported, 1 unsupported             │
  │  0.4 = Several unsupported claims                       │
  │  0.0 = Mostly hallucinated                              │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  LIMITATIONS OF LLM JUDGE:
  ❌ Expensive (extra LLM call per evaluation)
  ❌ Non-deterministic (slight variance per run)
  ❌ Judge bias (prefers verbose answers)
  ✅ Use GPT-4o as judge for GPT-3.5 outputs
  ✅ Always use temperature=0 for judge
  ✅ Combine with reference-based metrics
```

# 🏆 Which Metric to Use When?

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  METRIC SELECTION GUIDE                          │
│                                                                  │
│  YOUR SYSTEM             USE THESE METRICS                       │
│  ──────────────────────  ──────────────────────────────────────  │
│                                                                  │
│  RAG (Open-ended QA)  →  Faithfulness + Answer Relevance        │
│                          + Context Relevance (LLM Judge)         │
│                                                                  │
│  RAG (Factoid QA)     →  Exact Match + Token F1 + Correctness   │
│                                                                  │
│  RAG (Summarization)  →  ROUGE-L + Completeness + Faithfulness  │
│                                                                  │
│  Retriever            →  NDCG@5 + Recall@5 + MRR               │
│  (ranking matters)       (order of results is critical)         │
│                                                                  │
│  Retriever            →  Recall@10 + Hit Rate@10               │
│  (coverage matters)      (find ALL relevant docs)               │
│                                                                  │
│  Agent (complex task) →  Task Completion + Reasoning Quality    │
│                          + Tool Selection Accuracy              │
│                                                                  │
│  Agent (efficiency)   →  Step Efficiency + Redundancy Score     │
│                          + Latency P95                          │
│                                                                  │
│  Tool Usage           →  Tool Selection + Arg Correctness       │
│                          + Execution Success                    │
│                                                                  │
│  Production System    →  Latency P95 + Success Rate             │
│                          + Cost/Query + Retry Rate              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

# 📈 Score Interpretation Guide

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 HOW TO READ YOUR SCORES                          │
├────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│  Score     │  Meaning + Action                                   │
├────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  0.90–1.00 │ ✅ EXCELLENT — Production ready                     │
│            │    Keep monitoring, set regression alerts           │
├────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  0.75–0.89 │ ✅ GOOD — Minor improvements possible              │
│            │    Identify lowest metric, target it first         │
├────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  0.60–0.74 │ ⚠️  ACCEPTABLE — Needs improvement                 │
│            │    Not ready for high-stakes production            │
├────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  0.40–0.59 │ ⚠️  POOR — Significant issues                      │
│            │    Debug retrieval + prompt engineering            │
├────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  0.00–0.39 │ ❌ FAILING — Do not deploy                         │
│            │    Fundamental issues in pipeline design           │
└────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  IMPROVEMENT ACTIONS BY METRIC:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Low Faithfulness     → Better retrieval, stricter prompts
  Low Answer Relevance → Better query understanding, few-shot
  Low Context Relevance→ Better embedding model, chunking
  Low Precision@K      → Tune similarity threshold
  Low Recall@K         → Increase K, better embeddings
  Low Task Completion  → Better planning prompt, more examples
  Low Tool Selection   → Better tool descriptions, few-shot
  High Latency         → Caching, smaller models, parallelism
  High Cost            → Reduce context, use smaller model
```
